source.title: CAST: Continuous and Differentiable Semi-Structured Sparsity-Aware Training for Large Language Models
source.authors: Weiyu Huang; Yue-Zhou Hu; Jun Zhu; Jian-Fei Chen

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests a token-only loss scaling relationship and extrapolation in sparse-model retraining, a training regime distinct from the original dense pretraining scaling studies.
record.gate_note: The paper varies retraining-token budgets for fixed sparse model architectures and reports held-out WikiText perplexity, fitted curves, and extrapolation results. It does not sweep parameter count or compute to establish a compute-optimal allocation. The references to Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al. are not results from those studies. Zero-shot accuracy is discussed as not following the same trend, but the text gives no numerical accuracy results for this token-budget scaling analysis.
record.test_reason: Section VI-D and Appendix D fit a Chinchilla-style, token-only law L_i(D)=A_i+B_i/D^β to WikiText loss across retraining-token budgets for 2:4 sparse retraining of three LLaMA models. They report fit quality (R² 0.98–0.99) and a leave-one-out prediction of the longest run. This is a new training regime with its own result on the power-law form (V5) and on short-range extrapolation (V2). β is fixed at Chinchilla's 0.2849, not estimated.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that a token-only Chinchilla-form law (β fixed) fits sparse-retraining perplexity well (R²≈0.99) and predicts the longest run within 0.03. They use it to estimate the tokens needed for full recovery, which scale with tokens-per-parameter. The zero-shot caveat concerns that recovery-token trend, not a failure of accuracy to improve with tokens.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures token-budget scaling during sparse retraining of pretrained models, rather than dense pretraining loss scaling over parameter count, data, and compute. It fixes β at 0.2849 and fits model-specific coefficients.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted coefficients differ across model families; the LLaMA2-13B fit uses relatively few points and has a higher reported prediction error. The paper fixes β at 0.2849 rather than comparing fitting choices.

fits_no_version.finding: Predicted tokens for a sparse model to fully recover dense perplexity are 95.3B (LLaMA2-7B), 56.3B (LLaMA2-13B) and 1211B (LLaMA3-8B). The authors call this roughly linear in the model's pretraining tokens-per-parameter ratio.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Retraining cost to recover from compression grows with how heavily the dense model was pretrained per parameter.

fits_no_version.finding: Within the GPT-2 and OPT families, larger models lose less perplexity under 2:4 sparsification (Table V). The authors attribute this to larger models being undertrained.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compression degradation shrinks with model size or undertraining.

record.peer_reviewed: arXiv.org; submitted to IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence in July 2025
record.problems: The scaling experiment covers only three model configurations and sparse retraining, with token budgets up to 40B; the number of points is small for LLaMA2-13B. The exponent β is fixed from prior work rather than estimated or compared across fitting methods. No parameter-count or compute scaling sweep is reported, and zero-shot accuracy results for the scaling analysis are not numerically provided.

untested.parts: No pretraining-loss sweep over parameters, data or compute. Only retraining tokens vary, at fixed architecture.
Extrapolation by orders of magnitude. The tested step is ≤30B→40B tokens, and there is no parameter or compute extrapolation.
Shape and architecture are not varied at a fixed parameter count.
Other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer scaling. The exponent itself is untested because β is fixed.
Downstream accuracy vs tokens or loss is not analysed as a scaling relation.
No comparison of fitting choices. β is fixed from Chinchilla and A_i, B_i are fitted per model.

missing.what: Fitted extrapolated recovery-token estimates (95.3B, 56.3B, 1211B), which are themselves far extrapolations of the fitted laws
CAST zero-shot accuracy at 7.5B vs extended token budgets: LLaMA2-7B 55.91→57.52, 13B 58.75→58.93, LLaMA3-8B 58.38→59.43. Only two points per model.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. The scaling analysis is a side section of a sparsity-method paper. The reader's V6 'challenges' label is dropped: r23's statement is misread, and the label cited r22. β is borrowed from Hoffmann et al., so the fits test the functional form with a fixed exponent, not the exponent itself.

versions.untested_parts: The sweep concerns sparse retraining tokens, not held-out pretraining loss; parameter count and compute are not varied.
Tests extrapolation to the longest token-budget point in sparse retraining, not runs orders of magnitude larger in parameter count or compute.
No compute-budget sweep or loss-minimising parameter/token allocation is measured.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Tests sparse retraining only; no other modalities, repeated-data regime, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling law is tested.
The text states that zero-shot accuracy does not follow the token-scaling trend, but does not report the corresponding numerical accuracy curve or its relationship to pretraining loss.
The paper does not systematically vary fitting method, parameter counting, training schedule, or data to test fit-dependence or curve bending.

rows.value: Ai 1.561; Bi 0.258; R2 0.99; predicted perplexity 5.23, absolute error 0.02
rows.locator: Section VI-D; Appendix D, Table XII and text
rows.note: The predicted value and error are stated in Appendix D; the fitted token law uses model-specific Ai and Bi.
rows.check: Extrapolation runs from ≤30B to 40B tokens, a 1.33× step, not orders of magnitude. The fit fixes β=0.2849, so R² tests A_i and B_i only, not the exponent.

source_check.correct: V5: observed. V2: cannot_determine; the held-out prediction extends from a maximum fitting budget of 30B tokens to 40B, not orders of magnitude.
source_check.locator_found: Section VI-D; Appendix D, leave-one-out paragraph and Table XII.
source_check.problem: The reported values are correct, but observed overstates evidence for V2's orders-of-magnitude extrapolation.

rows.subject: LLaMA2-13B

rows.locator: Section VI-D; Appendix D, Table XII and text
rows.note: The authors attribute the higher prediction error as likely related to fewer data points.
rows.check: No numeric 13B leave-one-out error is given. The appendix says it is 'higher'; the main text says all errors are below 0.03. The fit uses only 5 points, all at ≤15B tokens. The R² of 0.99 supports V5, but the V2 state can't be read.

relationships.condition: 2:4 sparse retraining (CAST) of LLaMA2-7B, LLaMA2-13B and LLaMA3-8B, 1B–40B retraining tokens, β fixed at 0.2849
relationships.reason: Perplexity falls monotonically with tokens for all three models (r01–r18). Chinchilla-form token fits reach R² 0.99, 0.99 and 0.98 (r19–r21). The exponent was not estimated.
relationships.display_finding: Perplexity decreased monotonically for all three models, with Chinchilla-form fits reaching R² values of 0.99, 0.99 and 0.98 using the fixed exponent 0.2849.

relation.reason: It evaluates token-only power-law fits and held-out longest-run predictions using its own experiments.

tranche.reason: The study tests power-law loss scaling in a new setting: sparse retraining of pretrained language models.

source_check.notes: The synthesis statement accurately describes this study, but its placement under V2 support exceeds the tested extrapolation distance. The exponent was fixed; recovery-token estimates beyond measured budgets were not validated.
